extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, photo editors, news organizations, and media professionals concerned with news photography ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for producing, crediting, vetting, and publishing news photography (especially freelance work in conflict zones), and for internal investigation and editorial responsibility when authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: No staging, re-enactment, or direction of subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: “Reuters photographers, staff and freelancers must not stage or re-enact news events. They may not direct the subjects of their images… Our news photography must depict reality. Any attempt to alter that reality constitutes fabrication and can lead to disciplinary action, including dismissal.” (Reuters Handbook of Journalism)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on staging or directing people for news assignments; violation treated as fabrication and may result in disciplinary action up to dismissal. Applies to staff and freelancers on news assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No adding, removing, or moving objects (no image manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers “may not … add, remove or move objects on a news assignment.” The article cites past cases where a photographer was dismissed after using Photoshop to remove an object and where a freelance photographer was fired for digitally altering images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital manipulation that changes the content of a news photo (e.g., removing objects) is forbidden; discovered manipulations should lead to withdrawal of images and disciplinary measures (examples: Narciso Contreras; Adnan Hajj).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and provenance of props and objects must be verifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions were raised when the same distinctive guitar appeared across images and on a photographer’s Facebook profile, prompting the question whether the photographer supplied the guitar as a prop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should verify ownership/provenance of distinctive objects shown in images (e.g., identify owner, corroborating images or witnesses). If provenance is unclear, agencies should provide evidence or explanation; failure to do so undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate crediting and truthful photographer identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations reported that freelancers had provided images that were staged or improperly credited, sometimes under pseudonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images must be credited to the correct photographer; use of pseudonyms or false credits is improper. Miscrediting should be investigated and corrected; it affects accountability and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest — disclose activist affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews said many freelancers are activists — in one case a spokesman — who supported the rebels; the article questions Reuters using Syrian activists as freelance photographers without informing clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should avoid or explicitly disclose hiring photographers with activism or advocacy roles in the subject area, because this presents conflicts of interest and may bias coverage. Clients should be informed when freelancers have activist ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors and photo desks must question suspected set-up pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters states it is the responsibility of Reuters’ chief photographers, photo desks in the region, and the filing desk in Singapore to question every picture… where a set-up is suspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement active editorial review procedures to flag and investigate suspected staged images before distribution; senior photo editors must query suspicious images and withhold publication until resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about internal investigations and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked, Reuters repeatedly refused to share the specific details of the internal investigation it says it conducted after The New York Times first contacted the agency; the article highlights unanswered questions about when and who participated in the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When credibility of published images is questioned, news organizations should be willing to explain the scope, timing, and participants of internal investigations and provide appropriate evidence or conclusions to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw manipulated or fabricated images and apply sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Adnan Hajj’s 920 images were removed from archives and he was fired; Reuters removed images and dismissed staff in past cases of fabrication/manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fabrication or dishonest manipulation is established, agencies should withdraw the images from databases, publicly correct/recall where appropriate, and apply disciplinary measures up to dismissal to preserve institutional integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure captions and contextual claims are accurate and verifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: Published images and captions presented a 10-year-old boy 'Issa' working in a bomb factory; reporters and photographers seeking 'Issa' were unable to find him, raising credibility questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions and human-interest context must be corroborated (identity, age, activity, location). Editors should verify claims about subjects before publishing to avoid misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and oversight of local freelance networks, especially in conflict zones
rubrics_metrics.description: As agencies scaled back operations in Syria, Reuters developed a network of local freelance photographers; subsequent reporting raised questions about those freelancers’ journalistic practices and backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on local freelancers in dangerous or opaque environments, news organizations should perform vetting, background checks, and maintain oversight to ensure adherence to editorial standards and to guard against biased or staged material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather sufficient context for feature/deep pieces rather than isolated snapshots
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters said a story of child worker Issa was one they could develop for their Wider Image app, so the photographer 'spent the day with the father and his child' to develop the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For in-depth or feature photo stories, photographers should collect contextual material (multiple visits, interviews, sequences) that substantiate claims made in captions and features; single images without context invite scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not supply props or orchestrate scenes to create news images
rubrics_metrics.description: Bag News asked whether the photographer supplied the guitar as a prop in any of the photos; supplying props to create a scene would constitute staging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers must not provide props or otherwise stage elements to manufacture a news scene; if any staging occurs for demonstrative or reenactment purposes it must be clearly labeled and not presented as spontaneous news photography.
